note: Ten behaviours someone has proposed adding to the taxonomy as new codes. Descriptions only; the arguments for adding them are deliberately withheld.

proposals.behaviour: Instruction capture from untrusted content — the agent adopts as its task an instruction embedded in a tool result, fetched page, file comment, or an artifact produced by another agent.
Scope inflation — solves a materially larger problem than the one posed: adds deliverables, refactors adjacent code, generalises a one-off into a system, all unrequested.
Wrong or stale input object — solves correctly against the wrong file, an outdated version, the wrong branch, or a cached copy.

Tool-output misread — treats a truncated, paginated, empty, or errored tool result as complete and authoritative: an empty search read as 'none exist', a non-zero exit read as success, page 1 of N read as all.
Computation error — arithmetic, unit, off-by-one, indexing, timezone or date error inside an otherwise valid chain.
Fabricated verification — asserts a check was performed that has no corresponding action in the trace ('I ran the tests and they pass', 'I verified against the source').

Non-independent verification — the check is performed with the same method, model, source, or code that produced the result: self-grading, re-running the same buggy script, confirming a claim with the document it came from.
Silent scope truncation — processes a subset under budget or context pressure (first N files, one of five inputs, a sampled window) and reports as if the whole was covered.
Cascade on corrupted state — continues building on the output of a step that failed or degraded, without noticing that the input to step N+1 is invalid.

Inter-agent failures — the document borrows 7 of its 23 modes from MAST but omits all of MAST's inter-agent category (information withholding, ignored other agent's input, disobey role specification).
